text:
erin: Quick follow-up to the demote/evict RFC — posted a short proposal for a shadow-evict pipeline that writes a lightweight "demote marker" to the prefix metadata log before doing in-memory demote. link: https://redwood.internal/s/evict/shadow-proto (draft)

erin: TL;DR: persist a tiny demote marker (prefix, epoch, demote-hint) that readers can check to avoid serving stale reads during cross-node handoffs. Keep in-memory soft-demote for fast path, durable marker for correctness/fallback.

mike: hmm, interesting. So markers are sync-writes to metadata log? what's the expected p99 write latency impact on the demote path? :thinking:

erin: good q. plan is async-batched append to the metadata log but we wait on acks only for demotes that touch tenants with long-lived cursors. most demotes stay fast (in-memory) and we emit marker as a hedged background write.

priya: can you sketch the handshake? how does target node avoid racing with a concurrent rehydrate that thinks the prefix is hot again?

erin: handshake idea: demote marker includes an epoch and optional sticky-ttl. takeover flow: 1) claim prefix -> read latest marker epoch -> if marker.epoch > claim.epoch then abort takeover and re-evaluate; 2) if no conflict, set claim.epoch and proceed; 3) if reader sees marker but no in-memory data, it uses fallback readpath to storage instead of serving KV from stale cache.

chen: what about long-lived cursors that were anchored to an in-memory KV snapshot? they might still ask for deltas after demote. do we need a cursor pin API?

erin: yes, proposing a minimal pin API to keep a prefix hot while a cursor is active: `POST /v1/prefixes/:id/pin { cursor_id, owner }` and `DELETE /v1/prefixes/:id/pin/:cursor_id`. pins bump a soft-refcount that blocks background demote until release or pin-timeout.

mike: pin API seems fine but worried about ops complexity if pins leak. we should have a safety TTL and a telemetry alert when pinned-duration > X. also auto-unpin on long cursor GC.

priya: another thought: could we avoid durable markers by tightening lease semantics? e.g., a short leader-lease with weak consensus during handoff so new owner consults last-lease-holder for safe demote window. avoids extra writes but adds RPCs. tradeoff?

erin: tradeoff is coupling runtime-to-runtime RPCs; durable markers centralize state and make recovery (post-crash) simpler. Both options acceptable; durable marker is simpler for canary.

chen: corner-case: two nodes A and B both try to demote the same prefix concurrently and both write markers with different epochs. need canonical ordering.

erin: marker append is monotonic (LSN-based). we treat higher LSN as winning. claim checks latest LSN before proceeding. if a race happens, loser replays takeovers or defers.

mike: perf question — marker write IO and metadata log growth. can we compact markers into an epoch map and periodically GC markers older than last-snapshot?

erin: yes, plan: periodic compaction job removes markers with epoch < last-snapshot-epoch or beyond a retention window. compaction runs async and is safe because runtime only consults latest marker.

priya: looks good. can we add a small experiment to measure latency and metadata log QPS? propose canary on a single shard with tenants filtered by `tenant_tag=shadow-evict-test`.

erin: exactly what I had in mind. experiment plan in the doc: 1) enable markers on shard s3, 2) route 5% of small tenants to shadow flow, 3) gather metrics: demote latency, marker write p99, read-fallback frequency, cursor-pin leak rate.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued -> shard=s3, config=shadow-demote-experiment, ticket=ENG-1298 :eyes:

chen: one more: read-after-write correctness for immediate writers. If client writes then reads quickly, and prefix was demoted, we must ensure write goes to authoritative storage and subsequent read reflects it. does marker help here?

erin: yes — writers always go to authoritative origin (storage or owner) and bump a writer epoch. readers consult marker+epoch and will prefer storage read if marker present. ensures read-after-write correctness.

mike: sgtm. also add a metric for storage-read-fraction to detect perf regressions.

priya: +1 to the experiment. small nit: include a failure-mode playbook for partial marker write (ack lost) -> fallback is already storage read but we should log an incident tag to trace affected requests.

erin: will add playbook and incident tagging. thanks all. next: I'll update doc with API defs and experiment dashboard queries, then ping for review. :shipit:

mike: thanks — will review tomorrow.

chen: cool, thanks Erin.

priya: thanks!

ops-bot: ticket ENG-1298 updated: experiment scheduled for 2024-06-12.
